| Summary of Contribution:                                     |                |                  |                    |                       |               |      |
| **Role: conceptual design, Python prototype, testing and final report.** I drafted the Week 9 milestone proposal framework, including the problem statement, intended users, data requirements and business rules,  and designed the conceptual ER model. I produced the final ERD, including the overlapping IsA hierarchy, the ApprovedBy override relationship, the ShiftRequest weak entity with its Submits/ForShift identifying relationships and Reviews, and the ShiftStock relationship with a multivalued adjustment attribute, and aligned it with the implemented schema. I also produced the relational schema (RM) diagram, generated from the live PostgreSQL catalogue so that it matches 01\_schema.sql. I wrote the SQL queries and built the PostgreSQL database that the prototype runs on: the schema (16 tables with keys, constraints, triggers and three reporting views), the seed data, the twelve analytical queries (Q1–Q12, covering shift stock movements, dispensing estimates, latest counts, low stock, session demand, handover variances, rosters, purchase costs, attendance rates, expiry alerts and near-capacity sessions), the transaction and validation scripts, and a one-shot rebuild script with fixes for the booking trigger, UniKey format and identity sequences. I developed the Python command-line prototype (cli.py, services.py, db.py) and its README, covering student session bookings, session capacity management, cancellations, QR-token check-ins, end-of-day no-show marking, admin-override bookings, staff shifts and volunteer rostering, and inventory operations (stock counts, receipts and waste). Each operation runs as a single PostgreSQL transaction that rolls back on any error, and bookings use row-level locking to prevent concurrent double-booking and overselling. I worked on testing duplicate-booking prevention, the 50-student session limit, concurrent bookings, rollback behaviour and database integrity. I rebuilt the whole system on a clean PostgreSQL 16 database and confirmed that all 10 failure tests and all 17 automated Python tests passed (run twice to check repeatability), that the integrity checks in 05\_validation.sql returned no violations, and that the concurrency demo and CLI workflows behaved correctly. This review also identified stale figures in the earlier report draft and the limitations now documented in the report. I wrote the final project report in the official template: requirements, ER design rationale, ER-to-relational mapping, functional dependencies and normalisation analysis (3NF/BCNF trade-offs), integrity constraints, transaction and concurrency reasoning, testing evidence and APA references, and merged the group's edits. I also prepared demo notes on the system's limitations for the showcase video. |                |                  |                    |                       |               |      |
